Ocean Safety Bureau Officials advise no swimming at Hāʻena Beach Park due to shark sighting

HĀʻENA – Kauaʻi Ocean Safety Bureau officials are advising no swimming or other ocean activities at Hāʻena Beach Park until further notice due to a shark sighting.

OSB officials report that an 8-foot shark was sighted at Hāʻena Beach Park today, Oct. 20, at 8:45 a.m. No injuries were reported.

As a safety precaution, lifeguards have posted warning signs and will continue to monitor the area.

Lifeguards will reassess the area Wednesday morning, Oct. 21. Updates will be provided if more information becomes available.

For up-to-date information about Kauaʻi ocean conditions and ocean safety, please speak to a county lifeguard at any lifeguard station, call the Ocean Safety Bureau at 808-241-4984, or visit https://safebeachday.com/county/kauai/. View as web page

*Hurricane Lowell Recovery*

The County of Kauaʻi is partnering with Hawaiʻi Foodbank Kauaʻi to hold two emergency food distributions this week for residents affected by Hurricane Lowell. These are mobile pantry distributions. Please bring reusable bags or totes.

*Tuesday, Oct. 20*


* Anahola Clubhouse, 3900 Kawelo St., Anahola, 4 to 6 p.m.

*Friday, Oct. 23*

KEMA reopens FY27 Grant-in-Aid application period through Oct. 30

LĪHUʻE – The Kauaʻi Emergency Management Agency (KEMA) has reopened the application period for its Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Grant-in-Aid program, starting today, Oct. 16. The new deadline is Friday, Oct. 30.

New applicants are encouraged to apply. Organizations that have already submitted an application may submit an updated one if they choose. Previously submitted applications will remain in the applicant pool unless an updated application is submitted in its place.

The program is intended to benefit the people of the County of Kauaʻi by funding community emergency preparedness needs for which adequate federal or state funding cannot be secured. Proposals will be reviewed and considered for funding.

Funding is available through four opportunities across the following categories. Use the links below to download each application:

- Establishing and administering new Community Emergency Response Teams, or CERT (two separate funding opportunities, up to $10,000 each)
CERT Startup Application (PDF): https://www.kauai.gov/files/content/public/v/118/government/departments-agencies/emergency-management-agency/cert-startup-fy26-27-updated-oct-2026.pdf

- Providing aerial support for damage assessment, search and rescue, and public warning and notification (up to $10,000)
Emergency Management Support Application (PDF): https://www.kauai.gov/files/content/public/v/118/government/departments-agencies/emergency-management-agency/em-support-fy26-27-update-oct-2026.pdf

- Supporting sheltering operations as part of Emergency Support Function 6 (ESF-6): Mass Care and Human Services (up to $50,000)
Shelter Support Application (PDF): https://www.kauai.gov/files/content/public/v/118/government/departments-agencies/emergency-management-agency/shelter-support-fy26-27-updated-oct-2026.pdf

Eligible applicants include private and nonprofit organizations. Applications are also available at www.kauai.gov/KEMA under the Announcements section.

Proposals must be received on or before 4:30 p.m. HST on Friday, Oct. 30, 2026. This is a received-by deadline, not a postmark date. Proposals received after the deadline will not be considered and will be returned to the applicant.

Applicants will be notified of funding decisions on or around Nov. 13, 2026. The project funding period will run from Nov. 20, 2026, through June 30, 2027.

*Department of Water announces upcoming rate increases effective November 1, 2026*

LĪHUʻE - On Thursday, September 24, 2026, the Board of Water Supply, County of Kauaՙi, formally adopted amendments to the following sections of Part 4 of the Rules and Regulations of the Department of Water (DOW), County of Kauaՙi, for Fixing Rates for the Furnishing of Water Service in the County of Kauaՙi:

*_Section I. General Use Rates_* – Section revised to *increase Service Charge Rates*, amend Use Charge Rates from a Rate Block to a Rate Tier with increased rates, and add automatic annual Consumer Price Index adjustments.

*_Section III. Agricultural Rates_* – Section revised to *increase Service Charge Rates*, amend Use Charge Rates from a Rate Block to a Rate Tier with increased rates, and add automatic annual Consumer Price Index adjustments.

*_Section V. Private Fire Service Charges_* – Section revised to change wording to correspond with amended Use Charge.

The increase in service charge and use charge rates goes into effect on November 1, 2026. Customers can expect to begin seeing the updated rates on billing statements starting *December 1, 2026. *

DOW’s rates were last adjusted in 2014 and have not kept pace with the substantially rising costs of operating, maintaining, and replacing our water systems.  These adjustments align with those of other water utilities and, along with the annual Consumer Price Index adjustments, will help the department keep up with the cost of services.

The Rules and Regulations of the Department of Water, County of Kauaՙi, can be found in their entirety at our website www.kauaiwater.org/about-the-board/.

For questions or concerns about your bill, please contact our Billing section at (808) 245-5442, or email billing@kauaiwater.org. View as web page

DOW joins nationwide "Imagine a Day Without Water" to highlight water’s essential role Oct. 15

LĪHU’E – The Department of Water (DOW) is proud to join industry leaders, businesses, community advocates, and policymakers in recognizing “Imagine a Day Without Water” (IADWW) on October 15, 2026.  This National Day of Awareness encourages Americans to reflect on the vital role water plays in every aspect of daily life and underscores how clean, reliable water sustains our families, strengthens our communities, and fuels our economy. 

From brewing morning coffee to keeping industries running, water powers everything we do. It keeps families healthy, drives local economies, and helps our communities thrive. But too often, we don’t think about it until it’s gone — when a main breaks, a drought hits, or the tap runs dry. 

*“*Access to safe, reliable water is something we can never take for granted. Very quickly, we learn how indispensable water is in our everyday lives, and how our health, environment, and economy depend on reliable access to clean water,” said Joe Tait, Manager and Chief Engineer of Kaua’i Department of Water. “Here on Kaua’i, water makes it possible for our island communities to live and have life. Investing in water means investing in our future.” 

Each year, IADWW invites us to recognize how crucial our need for water really is by visualizing life without it, just for one day. Reliable water isn’t just about convenience; it’s the foundation of public health, economic growth, and community resilience.  

According to the 2026 Value of Water Index, most Americans agree that investing in water is essential. Support for prioritizing reliable water access reached a new high, outranking all other key issues presented to voters. Voters believe continued investments in drinking water and wastewater services are critical to support life – 96% believe these water investments are critical for good public health, 95% believe it’s critical for the overall well-being of their communities, and 85% of voters believe they’re critical for a strong economy. 

For further information, please contact Tiare Nichols at 808-245-5461, or email publicrelations@kauaiwater.org.

GD-PIO NR 10-15-26 (New lifeguard tower installed at Wanini Beach)
2026-10-16T01:58:36 [shelter]
*New lifeguard tower installed at Wanini Beach*

WANINI – The Kauaʻi Fire Department’s Ocean Safety Bureau completed installation of a new lifeguard tower at Wanini Beach on Thursday, Oct. 15.

“Our lifeguards are often the first line of protection for residents and visitors at our beaches,” said Mayor Derek S.K. Kawakami. “This tower gives them a safer place to work and a clearer view of the water at one of the North Shore’s most challenging spots. Mahalo to our Ocean Safety team for their persistence in getting this done.”

Lifeguards will now be stationed at the tower seven days a week, from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. The tower replaces the roving patrol the bureau has used to cover the area since the 2018 North Shore floods and landslides, which limited access beyond Hanalei and pushed more beachgoers to the beaches that remained open.

Wanini Beach is home to the “Back Channel,” an area known for strong currents and a history of drownings.

The $103,000 aluminum tower was purchased from Bausch Enterprises Inc. of Stuart, Florida. It gives lifeguards a higher vantage point to watch ocean conditions and respond to emergencies, and provides shelter from rain, wind, and sun during long shifts.

The tower was installed in-house by Ocean Safety Bureau lifeguards Kleve Zarbaugh, Gerald Hurd, Tyrus Siale, Eric Pereza, Christopher Davis, and Zackery Harris, with help from Department of Public Works staff Bryson Cummings, Lance Edralin, and Brannon Rivera.

“This tower represents years of dedication, perseverance, and our commitment to protecting lives,” said Ocean Safety Bureau Chief Kalani Vierra. “Our lifeguards now have a better vantage point to monitor ocean conditions, respond to emergencies, and serve our community and visitors.”

Vierra thanked the Mayor’s Administration, the Kauaʻi Fire Department, the Kauaʻi County Council, and the North Shore community for their support.

A blessing for the tower will be held at a later date.

Beachgoers are reminded to swim near a lifeguard and check daily ocean conditions at safebeachday.com.

For more information, please contact the Ocean Safety Bureau at 808-241-4984.

The new lifeguard tower at Wanini Beach on Oct. 15.

Ocean Safety Bureau lifeguards, from left, Eric Pereza, Tyrus Siale, Zackery Harris, and Gerald Hurd at the new lifeguard tower at Wanini Beach on Oct. 15. View as web page

*Oct. 19, Hurricane Lowell recovery, County of Kauaʻi services update*

LĪHUʻE – Please see the latest updates on Hurricane Lowell recovery and County of Kauaʻi services below.

*Hurricane Lowell Recovery*

*Emergency food distributions (NEW UPDATE)*

The County of Kauaʻi is partnering with Hawaiʻi Foodbank Kauaʻi to hold two emergency food distributions this week for residents affected by Hurricane Lowell. These are mobile pantry distributions. Please bring reusable bags or totes.

*Tuesday, Oct. 20*


  * Anahola Clubhouse, 3900 Kawelo St., Anahola, 4 to 6 p.m. 

*Friday, Oct. 23*


  * Hale Līhuʻe, 4286 Rice St., Līhuʻe, 4 to 5 p.m. Enter from the Convention Hall, then exit onto Rice Street (right turn only). 

To respect local traffic, please line up no earlier than 15 minutes before the start time.

*Hurricane resource centers to close after Oct. 22*

This is the final week of operation for the County’s hurricane resource centers. The final days of service are:


  * Kōloa Neighborhood Center, 3461B Weliweli Road, Kōloa: Monday, Oct. 19, and Wednesday, Oct. 21, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. 
  * Hanalei Neighborhood Center, 5-5358 Kūhiō Highway, Hanalei: Tuesday, Oct. 20, and Thursday, Oct. 22, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. 

Residents who still need help with Hurricane Lowell recovery are encouraged to stop by before the centers close. After Oct. 22, residents with outstanding needs can call 211 or visit www.kauairecovers.org for resources and assistance.

Mahalo to the staff, volunteers, and partners who served our community at these centers.

*Hurricane Lowell Business Recovery Grants*

The Office of Economic Development (OED) is encouraging small businesses and nonprofit organizations impacted by Hurricane Lowell to apply for financial assistance through the Kauaʻi Hurricane Lowell Business Recovery Grant Program.

The $2 million program, funded by the State of Hawaiʻi Department of Business, Economic Development and Tourism (DBEDT) and administered by the Chamber of Commerce Hawaii, offers one-time grants of $5,000 or $10,000 to eligible non-agricultural small businesses and nonprofits that experienced physical damage or economic losses directly caused by Hurricane Lowell.

Applications are open and will be reviewed and approved on a first-come, first-served basis until all available funding is exhausted. Eligibility requirements, grant details, application instructions, and the online application portal are at https://kauaibusinessrecovery.org. Applications must be submitted online. Assistance is available in multiple languages.


For more information or questions, call (808) 210-6839 or email lowell@cochawaii.org.

DBEDT will host a free workshop on Thursday, Oct. 29, at 9 a.m. at the Kauaʻi War Memorial Exhibition Center. The workshop will cover the grant program and other available business resources. To register, visit https://invest.hawaii.gov/dbedt-workshop-2026.

Agricultural businesses and producers will be supported through a separate state recovery assistance program. Additional information will be provided as it becomes available.

*SBA disaster loans for private nonprofits*

Following the federal disaster declaration, the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) is offering low-interest disaster loans to eligible private nonprofit and faith-based organizations in Kauaʻi and Maui counties affected by Hurricane Lowell.


  * *Physical disaster loans:* Repair or replace disaster-damaged property, equipment, inventory, and other assets. 
  * *Economic injury disaster loans:* Working capital to help cover operating expenses caused by the disaster. 
  * *Mitigation funding:* Loans can be increased by up to 20 percent of verified losses to make building upgrades. 

Loans are available up to $2 million, with interest rates as low as 3.625 percent and terms of up to 30 years. There is no interest and no payments are required for the first 12 months after the loan is disbursed.

sections.heading: Federal disaster declaration
paragraphs: The White House approved a Major Disaster Declaration for Hurricane Lowell on Wednesday, Oct. 7. The declaration provides federal Public Assistance to Kauaʻi and Maui counties. It does not provide money directly to individuals or households.

sections.heading: Visitor information on Kauaʻi Recovers
paragraphs: Visitors planning a trip to Kauaʻi or currently on island can find visitor information resources at https://www.kauairecovers.org/visitor.

sections.heading: Utilities
paragraphs: KIUC restored power to the majority of the island. However, some members in Kōkeʻe and other areas of Kauaʻi remain without power. Restoration in Kōkeʻe will take longer because of the extensive work needed there, and full restoration is not expected for several weeks. Do not approach utility crews or enter work areas.

Members needing a payment plan or financial help can visit https://kiuc.coop/payment-assistance or call (808) 246-4300. Collections for delinquent accounts are suspended at this time. Outage map: https://kiuc.outagemap.coop.
The Department of Water continues its Water Conservation Notice for customers in ʻAnini. Report outages or leaks at (808) 245-5444.

sections.heading: Refuse
paragraphs: Seven debris and refuse sites are open islandwide, with tipping fees waived for storm debris. Hours and accepted materials are at https://www.kauairecovers.org/debris.
North Shore refuse collection is on Thursdays. Tuesday service is no longer available.

sections.heading: County of Kauaʻi Online Services
paragraphs: As of Monday, Oct. 12, all County services, with the exception of DMV services, have been restored. The County’s online service portal, connect.kauai.gov, is also back online and available for public use. Residents with questions about specific County services are encouraged to contact the appropriate County department directly for more information.
The County of Kauaʻi’s IT Department continues restoration efforts following the Sept. 9 Kapule Building fire.

sections.heading: Contacts for County of Kauaʻi offices
paragraphs: General phone lines for most County departments have been restored. For the quickest response, callers are advised to speak to a live person rather than leave a voicemail. For a list of working numbers, visit https://www.kauairecovers.org/contact-us.

sections.heading: Līhuʻe Civic Center
bullets: In-person services at the Līhuʻe Civic Center resumed Monday, Sept. 28. County systems continue to be restored following the Sept. 9 Kapule Building fire. Services may be limited or slower than usual. Additional details will be announced.
Please call the office you plan to visit before going in. Working numbers are listed at https://www.kauairecovers.org/contact-us.

sections.heading: Building permits and storm repairs
bullets: The Building Division is open and processing permit applications, including those submitted before Hurricane Lowell and new applications. Service may be slower than usual while County systems are restored.
The Building Division counter is at 4444 Rice St., Suite 175, in Līhuʻe, open weekdays from 7:45 a.m. to 4 p.m. Planning staff are also available at the counter for zoning permit questions.
Pending applications will continue to be reviewed in the order received. Storm repairs covered by the emergency order do not go through the permit process and will not delay pending applications.
The online permit status lookup, Click2Gov, is available again as of Oct. 12. For more information or questions, call (808) 241-4854 or email building@kauai.gov.

*Most homes and buildings:* If your home or building was built with a County building permit and is not in a flood zone, you do not need a new permit to make necessary repairs for Hurricane Lowell damage. There is no fee and no County inspection is required, but work must still meet building codes. This includes building, electrical, plumbing, driveway, and sign repairs.

*Properties in a flood zone:* Contact the Department of Public Works Engineering Division at (808) 241-4883 or pwengineering@kauai.gov before starting work. Include an elevation certificate if you have one. Structures with repair costs equal to 50 percent or more of their value need a building permit and must be rebuilt to current flood standards. Stockpiling debris in a regulatory floodway is prohibited.

*Properties near the shoreline:* Repairs require a Special Management Area (SMA) assessment determination before work begins. The same 50 percent standard applies. Contact the Planning Department at planningdepartment@kauai.gov.
Property owners who would like an inspection of their storm repairs may contact the Building Division. Answers to common permit questions are at https://www.kauairecovers.org.

sections.heading: Real Property Division
bullets: Owners of storm-damaged property have until June 30, 2027, to file for disaster tax relief at https://www.kauai.gov/Residents/Report-Hurricane-Lowell-Property-Damage.
For assessment questions, contact (808) 652-7490 or rpassessment@kauai.gov. For billing and collections questions, contact (808) 241-4272 or rpc@kauai.gov.

sections.heading: Division of Motor Vehicles
bullets: Limited DMV staffing is available at the temporary Real Property Division office across from the Kapule Building in Līhuʻe and at the Kapaʻa Satellite DMV and DMV portable trailer at the Kapaʻa Armory, located at 4750 Kahau Road. The DMV portable trailer was moved from Līhuʻe to the Kapaʻa Armory on Monday, Oct. 12. Staff at these locations can answer questions and accept certain documents for processing once systems are restored.

*Notice of Transfer:* If you sold a vehicle, you can drop off your Notice of Transfer at the Kapaʻa DMV. Staff are entering Notices of Transfer into the system so records show the vehicle has been sold.
At this time, expired driver’s licenses that cannot be renewed due to the DMV closure will not be penalized.
Vehicle registration renewals are available online at https://mvr.ehawaii.gov/renewals/kauai/lookup and at community kiosks in Hanapēpē, Līhuʻe, Kapaʻa, and Princeville.

Kauaʻi County residents can use the City and County of Honolulu’s online portal to request a replacement or duplicate copy of a valid Hawaiʻi driver’s license at https://mydmv.hnl.info/hnldl/duplicates.

sections.heading: Kauaʻi farmers markets
bullets: Monday: Kukui Grove Pau Hana Market, 3 to 5:30 p.m., 3-2600 Kaumualiʻi Highway, Līhuʻe

sections.heading: Kauaʻi Bus
paragraphs: The Kauaʻi Bus resumed regular fare collection Thursday, Oct. 1. All passengers need to pay the applicable fare or show a valid bus pass, in line with regular fare policies. Bus operators and dispatch staff are on hand to answer questions and help riders through the transition.
The 900 and 950 Kauaʻi Bus express routes are not running.

sections.heading: County of Kauaʻi facilities
bullets: Open neighborhood centers: Kīlauea Neighborhood Center, Kapaʻa Neighborhood Center, Waimea Neighborhood Center (side rooms only; main hall closed due to damage), Waimea Smokey Valley Clubhouse, Hanapēpē Neighborhood Center and Multipurpose Center, Kalāheo Neighborhood Center, Līhuʻe Neighborhood Center (old and new), Anahola Clubhouse, and Kekaha Neighborhood Center (patio only for previously scheduled parties).
Wailua Golf Course is open for all 18 holes. The driving range is closed until further notice.
The Kapaʻa pool reopened Oct. 8. Waimea pools remain closed.
County park closures: Salt Pond (park and pavilions), Kaumakani (pavilion without electricity), and Hanapēpē Stadium (football field, pavilion, restrooms, and tennis courts).

All HI5 Redemption Centers are open. There are temporarily no Kauaʻi Recycles drop bins at the Hanalei Refuse Transfer Station. Recyclables are being accepted at Anaina Hou Community Park in Kīlauea on Tuesdays and Fridays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

bullets: Boards and Commissions meetings are scheduled to resume in October. A calendar of upcoming meetings is at https://www.kauai.gov/Government/Boards-and-Commissions.

headline.subject: NR 10-16-26 (KEMA reopens FY27 Grant-in-Aid application period through Oct. 30)

items.body:
KEMA reopens FY27 Grant-in-Aid application period through Oct. 30

LĪHUʻE – The Kauaʻi Emergency Management Agency (KEMA) has reopened the application period for its Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Grant-in-Aid program, starting today, Oct. 16. The new deadline is Friday, Oct. 30.

New applicants are encouraged to apply. Organizations that have already submitted an application may submit an updated one if they choose. Previously submitted applications will remain in the applicant pool unless an updated application is submitted in its place.

The program is intended to benefit the people of the County of Kauaʻi by funding community emergency preparedness needs for which adequate federal or state funding cannot be secured. Proposals will be reviewed and considered for funding.

Funding is available through four opportunities across the following categories. Use the links below to download each application:

- Establishing and administering new Community Emergency Response Teams, or CERT (two separate funding opportunities, up to $10,000 each)
CERT Startup Application (PDF): https://www.kauai.gov/files/content/public/v/118/government/departments-agencies/emergency-management-agency/cert-startup-fy26-27-updated-oct-2026.pdf 

- Providing aerial support for damage assessment, search and rescue, and public warning and notification (up to $10,000)
Emergency Management Support Application (PDF): https://www.kauai.gov/files/content/public/v/118/government/departments-agencies/emergency-management-agency/em-support-fy26-27-update-oct-2026.pdf 

- Supporting sheltering operations as part of Emergency Support Function 6 (ESF-6): Mass Care and Human Services (up to $50,000)
Shelter Support Application (PDF): https://www.kauai.gov/files/content/public/v/118/government/departments-agencies/emergency-management-agency/shelter-support-fy26-27-updated-oct-2026.pdf 

Eligible applicants include private and nonprofit organizations. Applications are also available at www.kauai.gov/KEMA under the Announcements section.

Proposals must be received on or before 4:30 p.m. HST on Friday, Oct. 30, 2026. This is a received-by deadline, not a postmark date. Proposals received after the deadline will not be considered and will be returned to the applicant.

Applicants will be notified of funding decisions on or around Nov. 13, 2026. The project funding period will run from Nov. 20, 2026, through June 30, 2027.

For more information, please contact the Kauaʻi Emergency Management Agency at 808-241-1763 or pgallagher@kauai.gov.

If you need an ASL interpreter, materials in an alternate format, other auxiliary aid support, or an interpreter for a language other than English, please contact Padraic Gallagher at the number and email above as soon as possible. Requests made as early as possible will allow adequate time to fulfill your request. Upon request, this notice is available in alternate formats such as large print, Braille, or electronic copy.

items.subject: DOW NR 10-16-2026 (Department of Water announces upcoming rate increases effective November 1, 2026)

headline.title: Department of Water announces upcoming rate increases effective November 1, 2026
headline.subject: DOW NR 10-16-2026 (Department of Water announces upcoming rate increases effective November 1, 2026)

items.body:
*Department of Water announces upcoming rate increases effective November 1, 2026*

LĪHUʻE - On Thursday, September 24, 2026, the Board of Water Supply, County of Kauaՙi, formally adopted amendments to the following sections of Part 4 of the Rules and Regulations of the Department of Water (DOW), County of Kauaՙi, for Fixing Rates for the Furnishing of Water Service in the County of Kauaՙi:

*_Section I. General Use Rates_* – Section revised to *increase Service Charge Rates*, amend Use Charge Rates from a Rate Block to a Rate Tier with increased rates, and add automatic annual Consumer Price Index adjustments.

*_Section III. Agricultural Rates_* – Section revised to *increase Service Charge Rates*, amend Use Charge Rates from a Rate Block to a Rate Tier with increased rates, and add automatic annual Consumer Price Index adjustments.

*_Section V. Private Fire Service Charges_* – Section revised to change wording to correspond with amended Use Charge.

The increase in service charge and use charge rates goes into effect on November 1, 2026. Customers can expect to begin seeing the updated rates on billing statements starting *December 1, 2026. *

DOW’s rates were last adjusted in 2014 and have not kept pace with the substantially rising costs of operating, maintaining, and replacing our water systems.  These adjustments align with those of other water utilities and, along with the annual Consumer Price Index adjustments, will help the department keep up with the cost of services.

The Rules and Regulations of the Department of Water, County of Kauaՙi, can be found in their entirety at our website www.kauaiwater.org/about-the-board/.

For questions or concerns about your bill, please contact our Billing section at (808) 245-5442, or email billing@kauaiwater.org.

items.subject: DOW NR 10-15-2026 (DOW joins nationwide "Imagine a Day Without Water" to highlight water’s essential role Oct. 15

headline.title: DOW NR 10-15-2026 (DOW joins nationwide "Imagine a Day Without Water" to highlight water’s essential role Oct. 15
headline.subject: DOW NR 10-15-2026 (DOW joins nationwide "Imagine a Day Without Water" to highlight water’s essential role Oct. 15

items.body:
DOW joins nationwide "Imagine a Day Without Water" to highlight water’s essential role Oct. 15

LĪHU’E – The Department of Water (DOW) is proud to join industry leaders, businesses, community advocates, and policymakers in recognizing “Imagine a Day Without Water” (IADWW) on October 15, 2026.  This National Day of Awareness encourages Americans to reflect on the vital role water plays in every aspect of daily life and underscores how clean, reliable water sustains our families, strengthens our communities, and fuels our economy. 

From brewing morning coffee to keeping industries running, water powers everything we do. It keeps families healthy, drives local economies, and helps our communities thrive. But too often, we don’t think about it until it’s gone — when a main breaks, a drought hits, or the tap runs dry. 

*“*Access to safe, reliable water is something we can never take for granted. Very quickly, we learn how indispensable water is in our everyday lives, and how our health, environment, and economy depend on reliable access to clean water,” said Joe Tait, Manager and Chief Engineer of Kaua’i Department of Water. “Here on Kaua’i, water makes it possible for our island communities to live and have life. Investing in water means investing in our future.” 

Each year, IADWW invites us to recognize how crucial our need for water really is by visualizing life without it, just for one day. Reliable water isn’t just about convenience; it’s the foundation of public health, economic growth, and community resilience.  

According to the 2026 Value of Water Index, most Americans agree that investing in water is essential. Support for prioritizing reliable water access reached a new high, outranking all other key issues presented to voters. Voters believe continued investments in drinking water and wastewater services are critical to support life – 96% believe these water investments are critical for good public health, 95% believe it’s critical for the overall well-being of their communities, and 85% of voters believe they’re critical for a strong economy. 

For further information, please contact Tiare Nichols at 808-245-5461, or email publicrelations@kauaiwater.org.

items.subject: NR 10-15-26 (New lifeguard tower installed at Wanini Beach)

headline.title: New lifeguard tower installed at Wanini Beach
headline.subject: NR 10-15-26 (New lifeguard tower installed at Wanini Beach)

items.body:
*New lifeguard tower installed at Wanini Beach*

WANINI – The Kauaʻi Fire Department’s Ocean Safety Bureau completed installation of a new lifeguard tower at Wanini Beach on Thursday, Oct. 15.

“Our lifeguards are often the first line of protection for residents and visitors at our beaches,” said Mayor Derek S.K. Kawakami. “This tower gives them a safer place to work and a clearer view of the water at one of the North Shore’s most challenging spots. Mahalo to our Ocean Safety team for their persistence in getting this done.”

Lifeguards will now be stationed at the tower seven days a week, from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. The tower replaces the roving patrol the bureau has used to cover the area since the 2018 North Shore floods and landslides, which limited access beyond Hanalei and pushed more beachgoers to the beaches that remained open.

Wanini Beach is home to the “Back Channel,” an area known for strong currents and a history of drownings.

The $103,000 aluminum tower was purchased from Bausch Enterprises Inc. of Stuart, Florida. It gives lifeguards a higher vantage point to watch ocean conditions and respond to emergencies, and provides shelter from rain, wind, and sun during long shifts.

The tower was installed in-house by Ocean Safety Bureau lifeguards Kleve Zarbaugh, Gerald Hurd, Tyrus Siale, Eric Pereza, Christopher Davis, and Zackery Harris, with help from Department of Public Works staff Bryson Cummings, Lance Edralin, and Brannon Rivera.

“This tower represents years of dedication, perseverance, and our commitment to protecting lives,” said Ocean Safety Bureau Chief Kalani Vierra. “Our lifeguards now have a better vantage point to monitor ocean conditions, respond to emergencies, and serve our community and visitors.”

Vierra thanked the Mayor’s Administration, the Kauaʻi Fire Department, the Kauaʻi County Council, and the North Shore community for their support.

A blessing for the tower will be held at a later date.

Beachgoers are reminded to swim near a lifeguard and check daily ocean conditions at safebeachday.com.

For more information, please contact the Ocean Safety Bureau at 808-241-4984.

The new lifeguard tower at Wanini Beach on Oct. 15. 

Ocean Safety Bureau lifeguards, from left, Eric Pereza, Tyrus Siale, Zackery Harris, and Gerald Hurd at the new lifeguard tower at Wanini Beach on Oct. 15.
